page: Microsoft Azure E8-4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.35 GHz. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 131 GB volume, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2706.38, while the Geekbench single-core score is average at 1597.0. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks are consistently weak, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is average for large block reads at 39.48 GB/sec, but weak for write operations and small block reads. This performance profile indicates that while individual threads execute efficiently, parallelized workloads are constrained by the low physical core count.

Given the high memory allocation of 16 GB per vCPU, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suitable for relational databases, caching layers, and memory-bound text or image processing tasks, where the 64.0 GB RAM capacity prevents out-of-memory errors. However, it is poorly suited for highly parallelized tasks, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by the weak multi-threaded decompression and poor 7B model text generation speed of 6.3 tokens per second.
